property_summary: The balance of any address never increases after a Collect call
The total sum of all balances never increases after a Collect call.
The total Ether held inside the contract (sum of all balances plus the contract's own balance) does not increase after a Collect call.
For any address that calls Collect, the balance of that address after Collect is at most its balance before Collect (i.e., the caller's balance never increases via Collect).
The balances mapping of any non-caller address never increases after a Collect call.
After collect, sum of balances and ether should not decrease relative to minimum sum condition.
After Collect, the caller's balance never decreases if it was below MinSum before the call.
After Collect, the total ether held by the contract plus the sum of all balances is less than or equal to the total ether the contract ever received.
After Collect, the CallerBalance >= MinSum implies that the caller's balance decreased by exactly the amount withdrawn.
After Collect, if the caller has a balance below MinSum, their balance stays the same as before the call.
The balance of any address never exceeds its maximum correct balance after a successfully processed Collect.
After any Collect call, the caller's balance never exceeds the stored balance difference before the call.
After a Collect call, the caller's balance is always less than or equal to the amount requested when the call does not revert.

After any Collect call, the total sum of all balances in the contract never exceeds the difference between the last successfully deposited amount and the last successfully collected amount for the caller.
After a Collect call that does not revert, the caller's balance decreases by exactly the amount requested.
After any Collect call, the total sum of balances across all addresses is preserved (non-increasing) in the reference, but the bug causes it to decrease.
After any Collect call, the sum of all balances plus the contract's own balance equals the initial total deposit.
After Collect, the caller's balance is exactly the previous balance minus the collected amount (i.e., bal[caller] after Collect == old_bal - _am).
After a Collect call reverts, the caller's balance decreases by at most the requested amount and never goes negative.
After any Collect call, the sum of balances[msg.sender] across all addresses is at least the sum before the call (non-decreasing); the bug causes it to decrease.
After any sequence of public calls ending with Collect, the value of MinSum is always the originally set value (not incremented).
After the contract is initialized, MinSum remains unchanged by any subsequent calls.
After any sequence of calls concluding with Collect(uint256), MinSum equals its last explicitly set value (not incremented).
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, MinSum is never incremented relative to its value after the last SetMinSum call.
The value of MinSum does not increase by 1 relative to its last set value through any public function other than SetMinSum itself.
The value of MinSum is never changed after initialization.
After Collect is called, MinSum equals the total value deposited by the caller before that call.
After an arbitrary sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), MinSum remains the value assigned in the first transaction.
After any call to Collect, the balances of the caller before the call are unchanged by the call to SetMinSum.
After Collect is called, the value of MinSum equals the value that was set by the first call to SetMinSum.
After Collect() is called, the state variable Log is unchanged (remains address(0) if never set, or preserves its previous non-zero address).
After a Collect call, the Log state variable remains unchanged (same as before the call).

After Collect() succeeds, the Log state variable equals the address that was last set by SetLogFile (or address(0) if never set), and the Log itself has not been overwritten to address(0) during the call.
After a Collect call, calling SetLogFile on the Log state variable returns a non-zero address.

After Collect() returns successfully, Log remains equal to the address last set by SetLogFile (or address(0) if never set) and is not overwritten to address(0) because the mutant always sets Log to address(0) on SetLogFile.
After Collect() is called, the value returned by the public getter LogFile() remains unchanged from before the call.
After Collect() is called, the value returned by the public getter SetLogFile() (the address stored as MinSum in the buggy version) is always 0 in the reference, but may change in the mutant.

After any successful Collect call, the address stored as LogFile (the state variable Log) has not changed from its initial value (address(0)) in the reference, while in the mutant it remains address(0) only if the fuzz _log passed to SetLogFile is address(0).
After Collect() is called, the public address returned by LogFile() equals the address that was previously stored via SetLogFile().
The value of the public state variable MinSum (which stores the minimum sum) is never changed by calling Collect().
The accumulated balance of the sender is equal to the sum of all deposits made by that sender.
After a call to Collect(uint256) that reverts does not change the message sender's balance
After a non-reverting Collect(uint256) call, the caller's balance in the contract remains unchanged regardless of the amount withdrawn.
The number of messages in the LogFile doubles when a successful Collect occurs.
After a successful Collect(uint256) call, the caller's balance in the contract decreases by exactly the amount collected.
After a Collect call, the sum of balances plus contract balance equals the initial contract balance plus total deposits minus total collected amounts.

After Collect(uint256) returns successfully, the contract's total ether balance plus the sum of all user balances equals the initial contract ether balance plus all deposits minus all collected amounts (conservation of value).
After a Collect call, the sum of all user balances and the contract's ether balance is conserved, but the rule fails if the mutant subtracts msg.value in Deposit.

After every Collect(uint256) call, the sum of all user balances recorded in the contract is always equal to the sum of all deposited amounts (from Log history or Deposit events) minus the sum of all collected amounts (from Log history) - but using a simplified invariants: the caller's balance after Collect is either unchanged or decreased by exactly _am, and never becomes negative.
After a Collect call, the caller's balance in the contract's balances mapping is non-negative and does not exceed the sum of all deposits made by that caller.
After a Collect call, the contract's balance equals the sum of all balances mapping entries.
After calling Collect, the balance of any address that just collected is decreased by exactly the collected amount.
After 'Collect' reverts (i.e., doesn't actually send ETH), the caller's balance in 'balances' mapping stays unchanged.
After a Collect call that succeeds, the caller's balance in the balances mapping is decreased by the collected amount.
The balance mapping value of any address is monotonically non-decreasing after any sequence of operations that includes a Collect call.
After any sequence of public calls ending with Collect(uint256), the balance of msg.sender in the contract is never greater than the previous balance minus the collected amount.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), the contract's total Ether balance is >= the sum of all user balances recorded in the balances mapping.
After any call to Collect(uint256), the contract's total Ether balance is equal to the sum of all user balances plus the difference between total deposits and total withdrawals.
After any sequence of public calls ending with Collect(uint256), the contract's total Ether balance is never less than the sum of all user balances recorded in the balances mapping.
After Collect, the caller's balance in the contract is never greater than before the call.
After any call to Collect(uint256), the caller's balance never decreases by more than the amount requested.
After any call to Collect(uint256) completes normally, the total Ether held by the contract (address(c).balance) never increases compared to its value before the call.
After a call to Collect(uint256), the contract's total balance (Ether) is less than or equal to its balance prior to the call.
After any call to Collect(uint256), the sum of all user balances recorded in the public mapping equals the contract's Ether balance.

After a call to Collect(uint256), the msg.sender's balance in the contract's balances mapping is always set to the same value as if the Deposit function had completed normally (i.e., the balance does not revert).
